strategy.summary: Reproduce sympy issue 27284 / PR 27287: Float(np.float32(inf)) and sympify of numpy float32 infinities raise OverflowError on the buggy commit fea3c41c1c7a in _convert_numpy_types (a.as_integer_ratio() on infinity); the developer test test_issue_27284 in sympy/core/tests/test_sympify.py should fail there and pass once infinities are mapped to S.Infinity/S.NegativeInfinity before the ratio conversion. Install sympy from the buggy checkout in editable/development mode with numpy present so the guard does not skip the test.

pinned_because: sympy==1.13.3 and numpy==2.1.3 are documented in the issue#27284 report environment (explicit, numerically relevant); python 3.10.15 is also from that report
numpy version is documented-pinned by the report, so it is relied on as explicit; the commit-message numpy guard is an installed-check only and does not impose a version bound
sympy version pin is informational: the repository checkout at fea3c41c1c7a is what is tested, so the buggy source must be built rather than the 1.13.3 wheel from PyPI

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision fea3c41c1c7a the test errors with OverflowError: cannot convert Infinity to integer ratio raised from _convert_numpy_types via Float(numpy.float32(float('inf'))), so it fails; on the fixed revision (PR 27287) Float(numpy.float32(float('inf'))) == S.Infinity and Float(numpy.float32(float('-inf'))) == S.NegativeInfinity hold, so the test passes. The transition is the outcome.
strategy.numerical_probe: import numpy; from sympy import Float; Float(numpy.float32(float('inf')))

input_output_examples.buggy_output: OverflowError: cannot convert Infinity to integer ratio
OverflowError: cannot convert Infinity to integer ratio

risks: The bug is platform-independent in principle (numpy float32 infinity on any architecture), so no special platform or sanitiser is required; however the test is guarded by 'if not numpy: skip', so if numpy is not importable the test skips and shows neither failure nor pass; ensure numpy is installed in the test environment.

The test file imports numpy as a module-level name in sympy/core/tests/test_sympify.py; if the repository's import guard is not present at the buggy commit, the test module may fail to collect rather than fail on the assertion, which would not be a clean transition.

numpy version unbounded by documentation or era table: the strategy relies on numpy==2.1.3 from the issue report; a newer numpy may change float32 handling of infinity or np.isposinf semantics, so keep 2.1.3 if possible.
Float precision of the returned value is not stated; the test compares with S.Infinity, which is insensitive to precision, so this does not affect the transition.
The reproducer snippet in the issue uses np without an import alias; use 'import numpy' and call numpy.float32 as the test does.
Editable install (pip install -e .) is preferred over pip install . so the buggy source is the one imported; installing the PyPI sympy==1.13.3 wheel would not reproduce the transition.

oracle.reference_source: developer test test_issue_27284 in PR 27287 asserting equality with S.Infinity and S.NegativeInfinity
oracle.why: The expected values are exact SymPy singletons, so equality is an exact check rather than a numerical tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The test calls Float(numpy.float32(float('inf'))); the buggy _convert_numpy_types calls a.as_integer_ratio() on the infinite value, which raises OverflowError before any comparison, so the test errors and fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the PR 27287 fix, np.isposinf/np.isneginf are checked before the ratio conversion and return S.Infinity / S.NegativeInfinity, so both equality assertions hold and the test passes.
